I'm 62 years old and I've farmed my 2.2 mu in Quzhou County for 40 years. I only finished primary school, so I don't read books about farming — I do what my father taught me and what I see working on my neighbor Lao Wang's field. My wife and I handle all the labor ourselves, and we pump water from our well when the crops need it.

The wheat is already in the ground from last October. I sowed an improved variety, same as Lao Wang uses — Jimai something, the bag just says "improved wheat seed." Before sowing I rotary-tilled the field and spread two 50 kg bags of 15-15-15 compound fertilizer across the whole 2.2 mu. This spring, when the wheat turns green, I will topdress with one 50 kg bag of urea. That's 150 kg of fertilizer for one small wheat field, which costs me nearly 300 yuan, but I would rather waste some fertilizer than risk a bad harvest. I will irrigate three times — green-up, booting, and grain filling — and spray pesticide twice: once for weeds and once if I see rust or aphids.

After cutting the wheat in early June, I will rotary-till again and plant hybrid maize. I buy hybrid seed from the town shop, Zhengdan 958 or whatever they have in the blue bag. For maize I will put down one and a half bags of compound fertilizer at sowing, and half a bag of urea at the trumpet stage. That's less than the wheat because the season is shorter and I have to balance my money — if I spend too much on fertilizer, I won't have enough for pesticide and the electricity to run the pump. I'll irrigate the maize twice: jointing and filling. Two sprays: herbicide right after sowing, and insecticide only if the corn borers show up, because chemical costs add up on a small farm.

I expect about 450 kg per mu from the wheat and 500 kg per mu from the maize. Last year I got about 420 kg from wheat and 480 kg from maize, so I'm hoping for a little more this year if the weather holds. I don't try new methods — if Lao Wang isn't doing it, neither am I.
